title: Ephemeral FD leak & kube-scheduler heartbeat jitter - investigation notes
body:
Summary:
We observed repeated kube-scheduler pod scheduling latency spikes across 3 clusters (prod-us-east-1b, prod-us-west-2a, staging-eu) over a ~36 hour window. Correlated symptoms: increased Pending pods, slow leader-election cycles for controllers, and node kubelet logs showing 'too many open files' warnings. Hypothesis: transient file descriptor (FD) exhaustion on kubelet/processes handling CNI/native dataplane sockets leading to eviction-like behavior and scheduler heartbeat jitter (controllers perceive nodes as slow).

Key signals observed (timeline):
- 2026-02-17 03:12 UTC: first alert - scheduler p95 schedule latency > 8s (baseline ~55ms).
- 2026-02-17 03:15 UTC: surge in node kubelet logs: repeated 'failed to open socket: EMFILE', 'accept: too many open files'.
- 2026-02-17 03:21 UTC: etcd leader observed short a 500ms apply latency spike (likely unrelated root cause but amplified scheduling latency).
- 2026-02-17 04:05 UTC: SRE oncall attached to node and ran lsof -p on kubelet and cni processes; per-process FD counts ~64k (open file limit 65k) for our custom dataplane agent; slab of /proc/net entries increased.
- 2026-02-17 07:40 UTC: rolling restart of dataplane agent on affected nodes returned them to healthy FD levels and scheduler latency returned to baseline.

Repro & investigative commands run:
- kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide (tracked p95 pending age)
- ssh node -> sudo systemctl status dataplane-agent kubelet
- sudo lsof -nP -p <pid> | wc -l (count FDs)
- procfs scan: ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l
- ss -s / netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT (look for socket churn)
- strace -p <pid> (short trace to confirm failing accept())
- journalctl -u kubelet -o short-iso | grep -E 'EMFILE|too many open files|accept failed'

Quick root-cause notes:
- The dataplane-agent has a bug where retransmit retry paths open ephemeral sockets (UDP + raw ARP sockets) and don't close them under heavy churn from multi-tenant sidecar CNI flows. The agent's keepalive/reconnect logic retries aggressively and leaks socket fds during backoff.
- Kernel FD table on affected nodes close to per-process RLIMIT_NOFILE (~65k) due to combination of: many conns from node-local proxies, ephemeral sockets left in TIME_WAIT, and leaking sockets from dataplane agent.
- Kubelet and system services sometimes hit ENFILE/EMFILE when creating ephemeral sockets or opening files for pod lifecycle hooks -> causes probe failures and delayed node heartbeats. Scheduler sees nodes as slower and increases scheduling retries.

Mitigations applied (short-term):
- Restart dataplane-agent on affected nodes (quick fix).
- Applied a temporary systemd Drop-In to raise LimitNOFILE for dataplane-agent to 200000 on 03 clusters (helps headroom but not a fix).
- Tightened CNI sidecar connection & idle timeouts for a handful of high-churn namespaces to reduce socket churn.

Observations from metric deltas:
- Node FD usage dropped from ~63k to ~8k after restarts in ~5 minutes.
- Pod Pending p95 returned to baseline after ~20 minutes on average post-restart.
- No increase in OOM or node-level CPU after restart (suggests leak was FD-specific).

Longer-term action items (owner + ETA):
- Fix leak in dataplane-agent reconnect path: PR reviewed by eng-networking (Ben Cho) -> patch scheduled, ETA 2026-02-25. (owner: Ben Cho)
- Add per-process FD watermark alert (new SLO alert): when any critical process > 70% of soft limit for > 5m -> page oncall. (owner: Ravi Patel, ETA 2026-03-05)
- Harden systemd service files for kubelet and dataplane: setLimitNOFILE to 200k and document reasoning in infra runbook. (owner: Elena Gómez, ETA 2026-03-12)
- Add synthetic probe that creates short-lived connections to dataplane and validates immediate fd closure (unit test + cluster e2e). (owner: eng-sre/ci, ETA 2026-03-30)
- Postmortem doc and RCA writeup for exec review (owner: Ava Martinez, ETA 2026-03-08 -> status: draft)

Open questions / TO INVESTIGATE:
- Are there kernel-level tunables (tcp_tw_reuse / TIME_WAIT tuning) we can safely adjust in prod to reduce socket table pressure? pros/cons?
- Is the dataplane-agent leak present on all versions or introduced post v1.9.3? Need bisect across canary nodes.
- Should we move to global iptables/nft based rate limiting to dampen sidecar churn rather than changing all sidecars?

Playbook draft (emergency runbook steps for oncall):
1) Alert triggers: scheduler.p95_schedule_latency > 3s AND Node.Kubelet.EMFILE log seen on >=2 nodes in a region -> escalate to SRE.
2) Run quick triage: kubectl top nodes; check /proc/<kubelet_pid>/fd; check dataplane-agent fd count; check ss -s.
3) If dataplane-agent FDs > 85% of soft limit: restart dataplane-agent on 2-3 nodes (rolling) + raise LimitNOFILE temporarily.
4) If restart doesn't reduce FD counts within 10 min: cordon and drain 1 node and collect full traces (strace -ff, lsof -p, /proc/net/tcp).
5) Apply temporary config (sidecar timeout) via kustomize to high-churn namespaces.
6) After recovery: collect logs, take snapshots of /proc/<pid>/fd counts, attach to JIRA ticket, and start RCA.

Notes to self (loose):
- Avoid mass restarting kubelet except as last resort; restarting dataplane-agent is lower blast radius.
- Need a small test harness to deliberately simulate 10k short-lived socket connections and watch FD accounting per process -> add to stress-suite.
- Consider automating temporary LimitNOFILE bump with a safe guard (auto-quarantine if process continues leaking).

Related artifacts and links:
- Heap of lsof outputs and node-specific traces attached to JIRA-OPS-1284 (see linked_artifacts).
- Temporary systemd drop-in implemented: /etc/systemd/system/dataplane-agent.service.d/limitnofile.conf (patch in PR linked).

Conclusion:
This incident was caused primarily by an FD leak in our dataplane agent under high connection churn combined with conservative per-process FD limits. Immediate recovery is reliable via agent restart and temporary LimitNOFILE bump. We need code fix, alerts, harass tests, and runbook updates to avoid recurrence.
